title: Magnetic quadrupole current generation and accumulation in noncentrosymmetric systems
abstract: Magnetization control via magnetic octupole injection has recently been proposed for a new class of centrosymmetric antiferromagnets, namely $d$-wave altermagnets, where the magnetic octupole is the lowest-rank magnetic multipole allowed by symmetry and serves as an alternative carrier to spin injection. In contrast, in noncentrosymmetric antiferromagnets, the magnetic quadrupole (MQ) constitutes the lowest-rank symmetry-allowed magnetic multipole, suggesting that MQ currents can provide an efficient route toward magnetization control through MQ injection. Here, we establish the symmetry conditions for MQ-current generation by constructing the multipole representation of the MQ conductivity tensor and show that MQ currents are generically allowed in noncentrosymmetric crystallographic point groups. As a representative example, we demonstrate MQ-current generation in the linear-response regime associated with symmetry lowering from the centrosymmetric point group ($mmm$) to its noncentrosymmetric subgroup ($mm2$). Furthermore, we reveal MQ accumulation near sample edges, analogous to spin accumulation induced by the spin Hall effect. This edge accumulation provides direct evidence of MQ-current generation and constitutes a key prerequisite for realizing MQ injection and MQ-based magnetization control in noncentrosymmetric antiferromagnets.
summary: This paper theoretically establishes that magnetic quadrupole (MQ) currents can be generated and accumulated in noncentrosymmetric antiferromagnets, providing a novel pathway for controlling magnetization. Using advanced group theory and multipole expansions, the authors prove that this effect is intrinsically linked to the breaking of spatial inversion symmetry. This work provides a crucial theoretical framework for designing MQ-based spintronic devices.
main_problem: The study investigates magnetic quadrupole (MQ) current generation and accumulation in noncentrosymmetric antiferromagnets as a mechanism for controlling magnetization.
main_result: MQ currents are generically allowed in noncentrosymmetric systems because the relevant conductivity tensor vanishes in centrosymmetric materials. The authors establish a framework showing MQ accumulation at sample edges, analogous to the spin Hall effect.
method: The analysis employs symmetry group theory and multipole representation techniques (Kubo formula) to classify the components of the MQ conductivity tensor ($\sigma_{n\alpha i;j}$).
model_or_system: The focus is on noncentrosymmetric antiferromagnets, where the magnetic quadrupole moment constitutes the lowest-rank symmetry-allowed magnetic multipole for magnetization control.
key_observables: MQ conductivity tensor ($\sigma_{n\alpha i;j}$), MQ current ($J_{n\alpha i}$), and MQ accumulation near sample edges.
important_parameters: The analysis depends critically on the crystal point group symmetry, specifically comparing centrosymmetric vs. noncentrosymmetric subgroups (e.g., $mmm$ to $mm2$).
main_assumptions: The study operates within the linear-response regime initially but extends to analyze non-equilibrium accumulation effects.
figures_summary: Notes mention figures illustrating the layer dependence of spin response in the mm2 phase and general references to tables summarizing multipole parities and conductivity components for various CPGs.
paper_structure: The paper systematically establishes symmetry conditions for MQ current generation by constructing the multipole representation of the MQ conductivity tensor, demonstrating its necessity in parity-broken systems, and predicting edge accumulation effects.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the rigorous application of group theory to classify emergent transport responses (like quadrupole currents) provides powerful theoretical tools applicable to understanding symmetry breaking in complex quantum materials relevant to AMO physics.
